WMT.rationale: Walmart is a best-in-class franchise with wide moat, 26.3% U.S. grocery share, $150B+ e-commerce, and a fast-growing $6.4B advertising business. However, the fundamental trajectory is mixed: YoY growth is solid (+7.3% revenue, +19.6% EPS) but sequential earnings have declined three quarters ($0.88→$0.77→$0.67), partly reflecting seasonality (Q1 is historically the weakest quarter — Q1 FY2025 was also lowest at $0.56). OCF at $4.74B is the weakest in the sample, a yellow flag. Operating margin is essentially flat (~4.2% vs ~4.3% YoY, above Q2 2025's 4.1% per the advisory correction). Valuation has compressed meaningfully — PE from 53.8x to 38.8x, near the floor of its 37.6–55.4x range — but at 2.6% earnings yield vs 4.54% 10Y Treasury, the stock still demands significant growth certainty. The oil price collapse (-32.7% to $73.15) is a genuine unpriced tailwind for margins. JPMorgan's $137 PT and August 20 earnings provide a near-term catalyst, but Cleveland Research's same-store-sales deceleration flag and China food safety scrutiny add risk. Net: high-quality franchise at a more reasonable but still premium valuation, with mixed near-term trajectory and a binary earnings event ahead. Mildly attractive, tempered by valuation and sequential uncertainty.
key_factors: Durable wide-moat franchise: 26.3% U.S. grocery share, 90% of U.S. population within 10 miles, $150.4B e-commerce (24% YoY growth), $6.4B advertising business (+46% YoY)
YoY fundamentals solid: Q1 FY2027 revenue $177.75B (+7.3% YoY), EPS $0.67 (+19.6% YoY), net income $5.49B (+18.3% YoY), net margin improved to 3.2%
Sequential earnings declining: EPS $0.88→$0.77→$0.67 over three quarters, though partly seasonal (Q1 historically weakest); OCF $4.74B is lowest in 4-quarter sample
Valuation compressed to low end of own range: PE 38.82x (range 37.6–55.4x), P/B 8.915x (range 8.4–12.0x), but still at 2.6% earnings yield vs 4.54% 10Y Treasury — 194bps below risk-free
Oil price collapse (-32.7% to $73.15) is an unpriced tailwind for transportation/logistics margins in coming quarters
Near-term catalyst: August 20 earnings report; JPMorgan projects $0.74 EPS on ~$187B revenue with $137 PT (~25% upside)

Risks: Cleveland Research flag on slowing U.S. same-store sales and inventory clearance pricing; China food safety regulatory action on Sam's Club; operating margin flat-to-declining despite revenue growth
ROE of 23% with expanding equity base ($90.34B→$100.68B YoY); liabilities-to-equity 1.88x elevated but typical for large retailer

sources_cited.excerpt: Walmart's leading 31% online grocery share and 20% digital penetration underscore the effective conversion of its store scale into digital traction.
Walmart online revenue totaled $150.4 billion in FY2026, up 24.4% YoY… Walmart's 5-year annual revenue growth rate is 5.00%.
Walmart's global advertising business grew 46% to nearly $6.4 billion in FY2026… Walmart Connect, the U.S. advertising platform, grew 41% in Q4 FY26.
90% of the U.S. population lives within 10 miles of a Walmart store, providing unmatched accessibility.
Walmart shares fell 4.5% after Cleveland Research issued a negative note citing slower same-store sales and concerns about the company lowering prices to clear excess inventory.
China's market regulator has ordered strict measures by Walmart supermarket chain Sam's Club to eliminate food safety risks throughout its supply chain.
Walmart currently trades at about 38.1x earnings, well above the Consumer Retailing industry average of 18.5x and also above the peer group average of 24.6x.
A low net margin (~3.1%) limits earnings sensitivity to revenue growth and leaves little buffer for cost inflation, wage pressure, or pricing regulation.
